## What was reported (EI-18783407644768125)

An agent loaded `coord:send`'s schema via `ToolSearch({query:"select:mcp__papercusp-su__coord_send"})`
in a cold-wake CLI process at ~07:50Z on 2026-07-27. The schema it got back
advertised the OLD, removed `expectsReply` field and did **not** contain
`expects` at all. A call built faithfully from that advertised schema was
refused server-side: `expects` is required (D-048), no default. The agent
recovered in one retry from the (excellent) error message, but flagged that
the published and validating schemas disagreed in the same live process, and
asked whoever picked it up to settle which of two mechanisms was responsible
before proposing a fix:

- **(a)** the ToolSearch deferred-tool index is a snapshot not rebuilt on a
  tool-definition hot-reload, or
- **(b)** the MCP `inputSchema` is generated separately from the parsing
  schema and the two structurally drift.

## Settled: (a), not (b) — reproduced live

A fresh `ToolSearch({query:"select:mcp__papercusp-su__coord_send"})` call in a
**different, freshly-connected** session (same day, same running operator)
returned the **current, correct** schema: `expects` present, `enum:
["ack","answer","action","none"]`, description leading with "REQUIRED",
`expectsReply` nowhere in the schema. This rules out (b) as a generation
defect — `toArgsJsonSchema` (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts`) calls
Zod 4's `toJSONSchema` fresh, with no caching layer sitting between a tool's
currently-registered `args` schema and what gets served; it faithfully
reflects whatever `send.ts` currently exports.

What actually happened: the agent's session had been connected (MCP
`tools/list` fetched once at connect) from **before** the D-048 code change
took effect for that operator process (this dev box hot-reloads tool
definitions in-process via `PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`, without restarting —
see `CLAUDE.md` § Prompts are auto-generated). Its cached tools/list snapshot
was simply older than the running code.

## Why an already-connected session never gets told to refresh

`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/transport/_mcp-handler.ts`
declares `tools: { listChanged: true }` and fires
`notifications/tools/list_changed` from exactly one call site: `activateTools`
(`ctx.activateTools`, driven by `tools:find`), when a **seeded** session's tool
**surface grows** (a previously-invisible tool becomes callable). That is the
*only* trigger. Two consequences:

1. **It never fires for an existing, already-visible tool's schema CONTENT
   changing** — only for a tool becoming newly visible. A hot-reload edit to
   `send.ts`'s `args` schema does not touch surface membership, so no
   notification is sent to anyone because of it.
2. **Claude sessions are explicitly exempted even from that**: "Claude is
   never sent the notification (it launches un-seeded → no surface → no
   fire)" (`_mcp-handler.ts` ~L1294). Claude gets the full catalog directly in
   `tools/list` at connect and is expected to keep re-deriving from that one
   snapshot for the rest of the session's life; `ToolSearch`'s deferred-tool
   index is built from that same one-time snapshot.

So for a Claude/psu session specifically, `tools/list` (and therefore
ToolSearch's index) is fixed for the **entire lifetime of the MCP
connection**, with no in-repo mechanism to refresh it short of a fresh
connection. A normal `:3070`/`:3170` service restart (a real deploy) drops the
connection and forces a reconnect, which picks up the current schema — so in
practice this staleness window is bounded by **dev-mode in-process hot-reload
without a restart**, which is exactly this box's normal edit-loop.

## Why this is not (and should not become) "fix schema generation" work

The reported symptom (a field silently missing from the advertised schema)
made this look like (b) — a structural JSON-Schema-vs-Zod-validation drift.
It is worth checking that hypothesis for any given tool, because a real
version of it *does* exist, deliberately, elsewhere in the same file: `to`,
`summary`, and `expects` are all `.optional()` on `coord:send`'s top-level
object schema (so an `items[]`-only call need not carry them), with the
single-message form's true requirement enforced imperatively inside a
`z.preprocess` (see the `D-048` / `D-016` comments at
`coordination/tools/send.ts` ~L1224-1268; `work_items:set_state` uses the same
pattern for its own shorthand-vs-structured duality, P-005/D-006). That
tradeoff is intentional, documented, and already covered by direct
`tool.args.safeParse` tests in `send.test.ts` (`describe('coord:send
`expects` gate ...')`) — a blanket "published `required` set must equal
runtime-enforced required set" test, as the original ticket's recurrence-guard
suggestion proposed, would immediately false-positive against this legitimate
pattern and any other tool built the same way. Don't add that test catalog-wide;
if you want a guard for a *specific* tool's shorthand-required field, assert
against `tool.args.safeParse` (as `send.test.ts` already does), not against the
generated JSON Schema's `required` array.

## What to do when you hit this

- A schema that looks wrong/stale for a tool you *just* loaded via ToolSearch,
  in a session that has been running a while: suspect connection-time
  staleness first, especially on a dev box with `PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`.
  Confirm by loading the same tool's schema from a **fresh** session/process —
  if that shows the current, correct shape, the mismatch was staleness, not a
  live bug.
- Read the server's validation error carefully before re-filing — as this
  ticket itself noted, the message is usually complete enough to recover from
  in one retry (self-healing), which is why this class of defect is "major but
  not critical."
- Don't propose a catalog-wide published-schema-equals-parse-schema equality
  test without first checking whether the tool uses the intentional
  shorthand/items-duality pattern above — it is not unique to `coord:send`.
